key_questions.answer: The FQ2 guide midpoint most likely lands around $100-104m. That is at the ~$102.0m middle of the three estimates but below the $105.6m headline mean, which a $115.0m estimate inflates. RGP's own arithmetic: the FQ1 guide's per-day run rate ($99.5m over ~63 US business days, $1.579m/day) applied to ~62.5 FQ2 days with a 0-5% fall uplift and a 0 to -2% trend gives $96.7-103.6m. Only the two-year-stack view ($105.8m) supports the mean. Management itself placed the payoff from its investments in 2H FY27 and said new sales hires take 6-9 months to reach quota. Against that, every staffing series published since RGP's July 22 guide points to a stable-to-better environment into FQ2, which makes a July-style step-down below ~$98m less likely than the tape implies. Versus the priced answer: slightly below the headline mean, about equal to the realistic middle estimate, and better than the stock's pricing of another step-down. The industry evidence is fresher than RGP's last call; the company-level evidence is RGP's own July numbers.

findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: The FQ2 revenue guide most likely lands at a $100-104m midpoint. RGP's own per-day run rate from the FQ1 guide gives $96.7-103.6m. That is around the ~$102m middle estimate but below the $105.6m headline consensus, which a $115.0m outlier inflates, so the guide is likely to print as 'below consensus'. Staffing data since July 22 (ASA +3.3-5.5% y/y, Robert Half guiding Jul-Sep talent solutions +1-5%, Korn Ferry interim 'significant lift') make a July-style step-down below ~$98m less likely than the tape implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Next-quarter guide: Jan 2026 -14.6% and Jul 2026 -18.4% when the guide stepped down after in-line quarters; Apr 2026 -1.4% on a roughly flat FQ4 guide ($104-109m vs FQ3 $107.9m), after which the stock rallied ~35% into June.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline FQ2 consensus the wires will compare against is still $105.6m. If the market and the vendors had absorbed the ~$102m realistic bar, the $115m estimate would have been revised or dropped and the mean would sit near $102m. Instead the mean implies +6% sequential growth that RGP's own per-day arithmetic does not support. Sized small because the stock at $3.69, below its $3.76 post-July close, already prices skepticism, and because the bar is single-sourced.
findings.independence: RGP's own revenue history and guide (https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK0001084765/us-gaap/RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax.json; https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2946047) give the per-day arithmetic. The offsetting industry series (https://americanstaffing.net/posts/category/staffing-index/; the Robert Half and Korn Ferry documents) are proxies, and RGP's -18% decline against Robert Half's flat F&A shows transmission is weak.
